# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-11

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero earns the click — the "47 + 28 = 76" example tells me in one
breath what Carnot does — but the page then squanders that goodwill: the
very first card under the headline throws three different AUROC numbers
(including a retracted one) at me, and the Evidence grid is a 12-card wall
of insider component names ("EstimationVerifier", "HalluGuard v3",
"VeriCoT") and implausible numbers ("35B model: 0% → 36%", "0.125 AUC
baseline"). A skeptical stranger keeps reading past the hero, then bounces
at Evidence because the numbers read as either broken or cherry-picked.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Implausible headline numbers erode trust — "Live benchmark — SOTA 35B …
   HumanEval pass@1: 0% → 36%" (a real 35B code model does not score 0%)
   and "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" (0.125 is far below chance).
2. The hero's first card self-undermines — "Recent progress" surfaces
   0.9131, 0.8947, AND a retracted "v2 0.9857 … repinned after adversarial
   audit" before I've decided to trust the project at all.
3. The Evidence grid is internal jargon, not landing-page copy — raw
   component/version names (EstimationVerifier, HalluGuard v3,
   IterativeSelfRepair, VeriCoT, PRM-BiasBench, CCTU, FoVer, k=5, pass@1,
   AUC-vs-AUROC) that mean nothing to a stranger.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Nav bar (lines 264-277) — 12 links — cap ~6-7. Twelve top-nav items
  (Get Started, Tutorial, Concepts, API, Problem, Capabilities, Results,
  Quick Start, Report, Paper, Writing, Roadmap) is a cluttered front door;
  a stranger can't tell what the one thing to click is.
- Results grid (#results, lines 517-578) — 12 result cards — trim to
  ~5-6 headline rows. Under the 20-card hard cap, but it is the densest,
  highest-jargon section and a stranger will skim none of them.
- Page overall — ~37 interactive cards across 8 sections. No single card
  exceeds the word caps (longest bento "Why Energy-Based?" ≈ 72 words,
  "Code" ≈ 62; longest r-card "Recent progress" ≈ 60), so the mechanical
  per-card caps PASS — the problem is aggregate volume + jargon density,
  not any one oversized card.

### Internal jargon
- Hero "Recent progress" card (line 312) — "5-seed dual-condition",
  "architecture-only 0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "pre-submission
  adversarial audit" — version/audit narrative a stranger can't parse, in
  the most prominent card on the page.
- Stats bar (lines 306, 308) — "382 Completed milestones" and "Verifier
  AUROC — FoVer math step-errors" — "milestones" is internal project
  cadence; "FoVer" and "AUROC" are undefined. "FoVer" recurs 3× on the
  page and is never once defined.
- Results card (line 549) — "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC" — internal
  class name + undefined dataset + a metric ("AUC") spelled differently
  from the "AUROC" used elsewhere.
- Results card (line 544) — "IterativeSelfRepair (HumanEval-50,
  execute-feedback-retry)" — internal class name + parenthetical jargon.
- Results card (line 559) — "VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix" — "VeriCoT"
  and "CoT" both undefined.
- Results card (line 564) — "PRM-BiasBench-style attacks" + (565) "k=5
  ensemble" — "PRM", "k=5" undefined.
- Results card (line 569) — "Cascade routing — HalluGuard v3" — internal
  component + version number.
- Results cards (lines 555, 560) — "pass@1", "TP rate" — notation a
  non-ML stranger doesn't read.
- Typed-constraints + tool-use cards (lines 451, 574) — "CCTU constrained

- Capabilities card (lines 497-499) — "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM …
  scales TTC based on Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance …
  intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — the single most
  opaque card on the page; spells out the acronyms but the sentence still

### Per-milestone narrative
- Hero "Recent progress" card (line 312) — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after
  pre-submission adversarial audit" reads like a changelog/retro entry,
  not landing-page copy. The version-history of a metric is internal status.
- Stats bar (line 306) — "382 Completed milestones" exposes the internal
  milestone cadence as a vanity metric; to a stranger it reads like sprint
  bookkeeping, not a reason to trust the tool.

### Inconsistencies
- THREE FoVer AUROC numbers in one card: 0.9131 vs 0.8947 vs retracted
  0.9857 (line 312), plus a separate "0.91 AUROC" prompt-injection figure
  (line 530). A skimming stranger cannot tell which is "the" number.
- Metric label drift: "AUROC" in hero/stats/safety vs "AUC" in the SVAMP
  card (line 550). Same family, two spellings, looks careless.
- Meter-bar semantics are inconsistent and visually misleading: "+3.0
  points" → 14.6% bar (line 521) but "+4.9 points" → 66.7% bar (line 526);
  some bars encode an absolute final value (0.91 → 91%, line 531;
  4%→12% → 12%, line 576) while others encode a scaled delta. No legend,
  so a bigger bar does not mean a bigger result.
- Section promise mismatch: "What you can check" / "Seven capabilities"
  (lines 415-416), but 3 of the 7 cards (Research operations, APIs &
  portable memory, TTC & PREM) are not things a user "checks" — the count
  appears padded to reach seven.

### Missing essentials
- WHO maintains it: only "© 2026 Ian Blenke" (line 762). One name beside
  "3,378 experiments / 382 milestones / 30,658 tests" reads as a solo
  automated/bot project — no team, institution, or backer for credibility.
- WHY trust the headline number: 0.9131 AUROC has no one-click path from
  the hero to its artifact/methodology, and the adjacent retracted-number
  mention actively reduces trust instead of building it.
- RECENCY: nothing is dated except the blog (newest 2026-05-23, ~3 weeks
  stale vs today). No "last updated" / release version. Ironic next to
  "382 milestones" — a stranger wonders if it is still active.
- SOCIAL PROOF: no GitHub stars, user count, citation, or "used by." For a
  research tool asking me to trust its numbers, there is no third-party
  signal.

### Fabrication signals
- "HumanEval pass@1: 0% → 36%" on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (line 555) — a 35B code
  model scoring 0% baseline is implausible; reads as a broken baseline
  harness presented as a Carnot win. Highest-priority credibility risk.
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" (line 550) — 0.125 AUC is far below
  random (0.5); either mislabeled or anti-correlated. Unanchored.
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (line 560) — perfect 1.0, no
  sample size.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (line 565) — perfect on n=60, no
  CI.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (line 540) — suspiciously exact 2.0×
  and "identical."
- "Zero false positives" (blog card, line 737) — absolute claim.
  None of these carry a sample-size or CI anchor on the card itself.

### Structural note (not in the six checks, but visible)
- The "Recent progress" r-card (lines 309-313) is nested INSIDE the
  `.stats-bar` flex row (line 304) alongside the four big-number stats,
  and there is an extra unmatched `</div>` (lines 314-316). It will render
  as a full text card crammed into a row designed for headline numbers —
  the one place on the page that likely looks visually broken.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero value proposition is genuinely excellent: the "Ask an LLM for
  47 + 28 … it says 76 with total confidence … Carnot is the second pair
  of eyes" framing (lines 293-332) is concrete, jargon-free, and instantly
  understood. Best copy on the page.
- Install path and license are obvious and repeated (`pip install
  carnot-ebm`, Apache 2.0 badge + footer). The "How it works" 3-step and
  the Evidence provenance disclaimer (lines 510-515) show honest intent.
